title: JSCG-P - Pre-Engineered Building Supplies With Roof Panels at Escuela Cosecha Amistad, Veracruz, Panama
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP). The Government is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing support in Veracruz, Panama. The purpose of this notice is to identify capable sources, assess industry capability and availability, and obtain industry feedback regarding the anticipated requirement. This notice is issued solely for market research purposes and to provide industry with advance notice of a potential upcoming solicitation. A solicitation has not been issued at this time. Description: Requesting a rough order of magnitude (ROM) for estimated pricing, and capability plan, to support the purchasing and transport of materials / supplies at Veracruz, Panama to construct a 11M x 15M x 5.5M pre-engineered building with roof panels. The materials / supplies are to be delivered on site to an elementary school in Escuela Cosecha Amistad, Veracruz, Panama by March 2027. Need the interior of the canopy to be clear space so the kids can play soccer / basketball. Request for Deliverables: Vendors submit a Technical Capability Statement illustrating their ability to purchase and deliver pre-fabricated building supplies across Panama Provide a general Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) outlining estimated costs for the purchase and delivery of the pre-fabricated building supplies at .Escuela Cosecha Amistad, Veracruz, Panama. If you can support this request, please submit the deliverables mentioned above by 09 Novembet 2026 by 12:00PM CST. Please email information to MAJ Vernon Shank at vernon.d.shank.mil@army.mil. Thank you for the support.

title: San Juan VAMC Construction Management Services
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE: The Office of Facilities Acquisition, Eastern Region, intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with AES Group, LLC, a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), to provide Construction Management Services for the DB renovation of the OR and Third Floor Corridor project at the San Juan VA Medical Center located in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541330 with a small business size Standard of $25.5 million. The authority for restricting competition on this requirement is 38 U.S.C. 8127(c), known as the Veterans First Contracting Program, which provides the authority to directly contract with an SDVOSB or a VOSB. The decision to make a sole-source award is a business decision wholly within the discretion of the Government. This Notice of Intent is not a request for quotes or proposals. title: H365--ANNUAL MEDICAL GAS TESTING POP: 11/20/2026 - 11/19/2031
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2025-06 (eff. 10/01/2025), FAR Deviation NOV 2025 (eff. 11/19/2025), VAAR DEVIATION APR 2025 (eff. 04/01/2025), VAAM Alert 26-01 (eff. 10/01/2025), and Acquisition Policy Flash 26-23 eff. 11/19/2025). This solicitation is set-aside for 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns IAW FAR 19.1405 SDVOSB Set-aside procedures, and VAAR Subpart 819.70, the VA Veterans First Contracting Program. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541380, with a small business size standard of $19 Million. The FSC/PSC is H365. The VA Loma Linda Healthcare System (VALLHCS), located at 11201 Benton Street, Loma Linda, CA 92357-1000 is seeking for a professional contractor to perform the annual medical gas distribution system inspection and testing. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: Supplies/Services Refer to Price/Cost Schedule (Attached) STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) TITLE: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) Annual Med Gas Inspection BACKGROUND INFORMATION: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) requires a new inspection contract for Medical Gas Distribution System. The Medical gas distribution system must undergo routine source and pipeline system inspections and maintenance to ensure continuous patient safety. OBJECTIVES: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) Medical gas distribution system inspections shall comply with NFPA99 (Health Care Facilities Code), OSHA Life safety fire code, and the ASSE 6000 standard. They require annual central supply checks, routine alarm tests, and specialized third-party inspections by certified ASSE 6020 Inspectors. The services performed shall conform to industry standards and this statement of work (SOW) and lockout and tagout procedures are to be done according to (OSHA Standard29 CFR 1910.147) VA Loma Linda Healthcare systems Policies and Regulations. SCOPE: Contractors shall provide all labor, personnel, supplies, equipment, tools, materials, supervision and other necessary items. Inspection, testing and verification are mandatory for medical gas work and will be performed by licensed ASSE 6020 Medical Gas Inspectors and ASSE 6030 Medical Gas Verifiers. Contractor shall perform Annual Medical Gas Distribution System Inspection on all Sources, Alarms, Zone Valves, and Patient Terminal Outlets / Inlets and bulk oxygen system. Including Areas as follows: Main Hospital First Floor: CLC, CLC Palliative Care, CLC Rehab, 1SW, Mod 3, Emergency department, Second Floor: ICU: 2SW, 2SE, Third Floor: OR 1 through 8, 3F-14, 3F-16, 3D-72, Recovery Room, SICU, X-Ray, MRI, Short Stay, G.I. Labs, 3NW, 3NE, 3SW, 3SE Fourth Floor: 4NW, 4NE, 4SW, 4SE, Nuclear Med, Dialysis, Blood Laboratory, Oncology Building 31 Eye Clinic Building 32 Audiology Building 30 List of items provided for inspection: Medical Gas Sources Medical air compressors, vacuum pumps, gas manifolds, and any other device used to deliver medical gases to patients. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Leak checked and documented. 3.Recommendations to comply with NFPA 99, 2024 edition Health Care Facilities Code. Master Alarm Panels Alarm panels are located at two separate locations throughout the facility. These panels monitor conditions directly from the medical gas sources. 1.Inventoried by location 2.Tested by removing existing pressure switches and other sensing devices to test the actuation points. No interruption of service is necessary if each device is mounted on code compliant demand fittings. 3.Verify proper points are being monitored at each panel. 4.Verify each panel is in the proper location. 5.Verify proper labeling. Area Alarm Panels Alarm panels that are located throughout the facility monitor medical gas pressures for the area only. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Tested by lowering pressure in each zone for each gas and documenting the alarm point. 3.Verify proper location. 4.Verify proper labeling. Zone Valve Boxes Accessible valves typically found in a corridor covered by a plastic window used mostly for emergency purposes. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Checked for leakage from packing, flange, and gauge port using oxygen safe leak detector. 3.Verify proper labeling. 4.Verify proper locations. Medical Gas Outlets/Inlets Connection points for each gas are located mostly in-patient areas. 1.Inventoried by location in each room or area inspected left to right and then top to bottom. 2.Complete an operational pressure test on each outlet and document pass/fail. (Test Parameters per NFPA 99, 2024 edition) 3.Check function of outlet/inlet and latching mechanism. 4.Check for leakage with equipment and without equipment attached. 5.Document connection type and outlet/inlet manufacturer. Oxygen Particulate Analysis Particulates are often found in existing medical gas systems due to improper installation methods that were used in the past. 1.Samples are taken on each floor in each building. Medical Air Dewpoint Analysis Moisture is removed from medical air systems at the source. Periodic Analysis of moisture throughout the facility is important to prevent possible contamination. 1.Samples are taken on each floor in each building. 2.A sample will be taken at the medical air source to compare building samples. Emergency Oxygen Supply Connection Box This box is typically mounted on the outside of a facility to facilitate the back feeding of the oxygen system if there is an interruption in service. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Check existing location for proper compliance. 3.Check existing piping arrangements to ensure proper order of components. 4.Check to make sure box is secured. Testing to ensure all medical gas booms, and columns are leak free Most operating rooms and procedure rooms have some sort of device to help clinical personnel use the medical gases in the middle of the room by the patient. These devices are either medical gas booms or columns. The hoses and threaded connections inside these devices need to be checked periodically to ensure that there are no leaks. 1. All hoses and secondary equipment were removed from the outlets on each boom and column. 2. A test pressure for each system was observed and documented. 3. All medical gas valves were shut over a period of 10 minutes. 4. After the test period of 10 minutes passed the pressure was observed once again. 5. Any pressure drop was recorded. 6. Recommendations will be made to find existing leaks and to make repairs. Facilities responsibility: A. The facility shall coordinate with all departments to notify of the medical gas/vacuum system inspection and or repairs to be completed. B. The facility shall supply Inspecting personnel with facility maintenance personnel to unlock secured areas that have medical gas/vacuum systems, or a master key may also be supplied to complete inspection services. REPORTS: The contractor will annotate compliance with ASSE 6000, 6020 and 6030 Medical Gas specifications and requirements by submitting a detailed PM report to the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) along with pictures for each equipment, after PM is completed. The reports shall be submitted to COR, within 14 days of work completion. The contractor shall provide additional reports as required by the COR. The c

description: This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice is issued for market research purposes only pursuant to FAR Part 10. This notice does not obligate the Government to issue a future solicitation, award a contract, reimburse respondents for costs incurred, or otherwise pay for information submitted in response to this notice. Responses will be used to assess market capability and acquisition strategy development. USDA is conducting market research to identify commercial, academic, nonprofit, and other qualified organizations capable of providing a fully integrated weather information capability supporting the Federal Crop Insurance Program and NRCS operational requirements. The Government seeks information regarding industry capability to provide an operational, nationwide, scientifically defensible weather information service consisting of weather observations, quality control processes, terrain-aware weather modeling, historical archives, analytical tools, geospatial products, public dissemination services, restricted operational services, scientific support, and supporting infrastructure as a single integrated capability. The Government is specifically interested in determining whether capable sources exist that can provide an operational capability meeting or exceeding the functional outcomes currently relied upon by USDA programs. The Government seeks capability statements from organizations capable of delivering a complete end-to-end weather information service that supports: Federal Crop Insurance Program operations Weather validation activities Weather-related underwriting and claims analysis Prevented planting determinations Historical weather reconstruction Program integrity reviews NRCS data estimation and quality-control operations Public dissemination of weather information Scientific analysis and support The Government is not seeking individual datasets, individual models, isolated software applications, consulting-only services, or limited analytical support. The Government seeks information regarding complete integrated capabilities. Required Capability Areas Respondents shall address their current operational capabilities within the following major areas. 1. Integrated Operational Capability The respondent shall demonstrate an existing operational capability providing: Ground-based observation acquisition Observation quality assurance/quality control Terrain-aware weather modeling Historical weather archives Weather product generation Geospatial services Public dissemination Restricted operational user services Analytical tools Scientific support Infrastructure and operations The complete capability shall be currently available. 2. Observation Acquisition and Quality Control The Government seeks information regarding: Use of federal, state, tribal, academic, cooperative, public, and commercial weather networks. Integration of NRCS station data from the Water and Climate Information System (WCIS) Air and Water Database (AWDB). Use of CoCoRaHS observations. Use of state and regional Mesonet data. Station metadata validation. Observation lineage and traceability. Automated and manual QA/QC processes. Observation anomaly detection and resolution procedures. Respondents should describe operational processes, governance, documentation, and evidence supporting these capabilities. 3. Weather Modeling The Government seeks information regarding operational terrain-aware weather modeling capable of: Incorporating elevation effects. Incorporating slope and exposure influences. Accounting for rain-shadow impacts. Addressing coastal influences. Producing scientifically supportable estimates in sparse observation environments. Integrating observations and model output into operational products. Respondents should describe model architecture, operational status, validation methods, and production workflows. 4. National Weather Products The Government seeks operational capabilities providing: Gridded precipitation. Maximum temperature. Minimum temperature. Products shall be available for: CONUS Alaska Hawaii Products should support operational delivery at nominal spatial resolutions of 800 meters or finer. 5. Historical Archive and Data Stewardship The Government seeks information regarding: Historical archives extending at least thirty years. Product version management. Historical reproducibility. Metadata preservation. Revision tracking. Product lineage documentation. 6. Derived Agricultural Weather Products The Government seeks information regarding operational generation of: Weather normals Ten-year averages Weather departures from normal Growing degree days Chilling hours Aggregated weather statistics Agricultural weather indicators Respondents should describe methodologies and reproducibility controls. 7. Crop Insurance Operational Support The Government seeks information regarding support for: Claims validation Underwriting analysis Prevented planting reviews Historical event reconstruction Authorized litigation support Program integrity reviews Convergence-of-evidence weather analysis 8. Restricted Operational Services The Government seeks information regarding secure operational portals that provide authorized users with: Weather reports Maps Historical analyses Downloadable geospatial data Raster-based analytical processing Repeatable analytical workflows Downloadable outputs Respondents should describe scalability, availability, auditability, lineage tracking, and security controls. 9. Public Dissemination The Government seeks information regarding operational public-access services that: Provide designated weather products without subscription fees. Publish historical and current weather data. Maintain public metadata and methodology documentation. Support public download of designated weather products. 10. Scientific Support The Government seeks information regarding scientific staffing and support including: PhD-level scientists with expertise in meteorology, climatology, hydrology, atmospheric science, agricultural weather, geospatial science, or related disciplines. Direct engagement with RMA subject matter experts. Direct engagement with NRCS subject matter experts. Expertise in weather observation systems, modeling, quality control, validation, statistics, geospatial analysis, and operational support. 11. NRCS-Specific Requirements The Government seeks information regarding capabilities supporting: SNOTEL SNOLITE SCAN including: Daily estimates Historical estimates API services Performance metrics Data lineage Estimation methodologies Quality-control portals Non-stationarity analyses Information Requested Interested organizations shall provide: 1. Corporate Information Company name UEI CAGE Code Business size Socioeconomic status Primary points of contact 2. Capability Statement A narrative describing the firm's capability to provide the complete integrated service. 3. Compliance Matrix Provide a requirement-by-requirement response for all mandatory requirements identified in Attachment 1. For each requirement, identify: Compliant Partially Compliant Not Compliant For each response include: Operational status Objective evidence Description of capability Dependencies Data restrictions Licensing restrictions Government-furnished requirements Transition requirements Staffing requirements Assumptions 4. Operational Readiness Identify which capabilities are: Fully operational today Operational with minor enhancements In development Planned / conceptual Respondents shall not represent conceptual or planned functionality as current operational capability. 5. Transition Approach Describe how continuity of operations would be maintained during transition while avoiding disruption to RMA and NRCS operations. 6. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Background: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Division of Police, is responsible for providing and administering contract guard services at specific buildings and entrances both on and off the NIH campus in the Washington-Baltimore area to supplement security systems and law enforcement personnel. To provide independent quality validation of this contract guard force, free of the bias inherent in self-assessment, NIH separately acquires performance management and surveillance services of the guard force vendor from a different contractor not involved in day-to-day security operations. This surveillance function is critical to validating that contract security guard services are performed at a continuous, acceptable quality level, helping prevent weaponized vehicles and unauthorized personnel from entering the NIH main campus and satellite facilities. There are currently 22 separate posts/locations on the main campus and 9 off-campus sites with contract guards assigned, several staffed 24 hours a day, located throughout the greater Washington-Baltimore region including Bethesda, Baltimore, Fort Detrick, Poolesville, and Rockville, Maryland. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of this acquisition is to procure surveillance and quality assurance services of NIH's contract security guard force, consistent with the Guard Force Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan / Performance Requirements Summary (QASP/PRS). Project requirements: Independently, and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall perform the following: Conduct random, scheduled, and unscheduled inspections/surveillance of the contract guard force at all NIH facilities in the Washington-Baltimore area with assigned contract guards, during all hours of the day and night, including holidays, weekends, and periods of inclement weather. Evaluate guard force performance across five categories: Access Control; Roving Patrols; Training and Recruitment; Professional Guard Service and Complaint Monitoring; and Continuous Improvement/Contract Reporting. Conduct surreptitious attempts to penetrate perimeter vehicle entrances and building entrances, including testing vehicle entry points from a vehicle operator's position, using contractor-provided and maintained vehicles. Report negative surveillance findings to the NIH Contracting Officer's Representative and Division of Police within 30 minutes of an observed infraction, with electronic data entry follow-up. Provide immediate/next-business-day written reports for reportable incidents (e.g., vacant posts, validated sleeping-on-post infractions, incidents involving designated NIH senior officials), plus weekly, monthly, and quarterly summary reporting. Provide personnel deployment schedules not less than two weeks in advance. Maintain staffing capable of maintaining telephone communication with NIH at all times while performing assigned duties. Document surveillance processes for each facility/location within 90 to 120 days of surveillance beginning at that location. All assigned personnel must maintain required security clearances, undergo background investigation, and comply with HSPD-12 requirements for access to NIH secure areas. Locality Requirement: Per the Statement of Objectives for this requirement, the contractor shall maintain an administrative office within 100 miles of the NIH campus, to facilitate regular coordination between the Project Officer and the Contractor. description: Dashboard link: https://geo-essayons.egis.usace.army.mil/portal/apps/experiencebuilder/experience/?id=1b5c149b77d04afa8aa97160476258d4 DRAFT RFP ADDED Special Notice: W912PM27RA006 Title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget will occur on 16 October 2026 from 0900ET to 13:00ET via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing Scope Dredge to Budget acquisition strategy. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 15 October 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026. There will also be a face-to-face meeting with individual contractors that have the required equipment and intend to propose on this future solicitation. The face-to-face meetings will be on 03-04 November in Galveston, TX. Please respond to to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil of your interest in a face-to-face meeting no later than 24 September 2026 at 1PM ET.

title: USCGC ASPEN DryDock Repairs FY27
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION; not a pre-solicitation notice or solicitation for proposals/quotations. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: (1) determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exists, (2) determine if commercial items suitable to meet the agency's needs are available or could be modified to meet the agency's requirements, and (3) determine the commercial practices of company's engaged in providing the needed service or supply. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. The US Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistic Center, Alameda CA is seeking contractors interested in providing Maintenance and Repair Services with DRYDOCK AVAILABILITY FY2027 for the USCGC ASPEN (WLB-208) FY27 Drydock Availability. The US Coast Guard Cutter ASPEN (WLB-208) is a 225' seagoing buoy tender homeported at: 4688 Homer Spit Road. Home, AK 99603. Work list will include but is not limited to: Drydocking of a vessel 225ft in length, inspection/maintenance/ and preservation of underwater body paint/hull/ and buoy deck anchor chain, maintenance to rudder/propeller/thrusters/ and shafting, cleaning of ballast/sewage/fuel tanks and piping, crane/deck equipment work, and renewal of sea valves and strainers There are approximately 108 Line Items. ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT*** 1. A WLB's design limits its use to protected and inland waters. The cutter is not crewed for continuous steaming and is normally limited to daylight transits. Due to crewing and cutter employment standards, seven days transit is the limit of crew endurance under normal operating conditions. Ten hours of transit per day is the planning factor due to crew fatigue. WLB's have a maximum speed of 10 knots, however, environmental factors frequently limit average speed to 6.5 knots. 2. Foreseeable costs (crew lodging, messing, rental vehicles, fuel, and authorized crew travel in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulations) will be added to the pricing and will be an economic consideration for award. CUTTER�S HOMEPORT: Homer, AK PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Contractor�s Facilities DESCRIPTION OF WORK: See attached (Rev-0, 01 October 2026) USCGC ASPEN (WLB 208) SPECIFICATION FOR DRYDOCK REPAIRS FY2027 ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL DETAILS*** ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 07/06/2027 � 11/07/2027 (125 Days) The applicable NAICS Code is 336611, Ship Building and Repairing, and the size standard is 1,300 employees. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Companies having capabilities necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements are invited to provide information and a positive statement OF INTEREST, to contribute to this market survey/sources sought notice including commercial market information and company information. Companies may respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to POC listed in the Contract Opportunities announcement with the following information/documentation: 1. Name of Company, Address and DUNS Number. 2. Point of Contact and Phone Number. 3. Business Size applicable to the NAICS Code: 8(a) Small Business Concern; b. HUBZone Small Business Concern; c. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (SDVOSBC); d. Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (VOSBC); e. ED Woman Owned Small Business Concern (EDWOSB); f. Woman Owned Small Business Concern (WOSBC); g. Small Business Concern; h. Large Business Concern. 4. Documentation Verifying Small Business Certification: Please provide the following documentation as it applies to you company. � If claiming 8(a) status, provide a copy of your 8(a) Certificate from SBA. � If claiming HUBZone status, provide a copy of your HUBZone Certificate from SBA. � If claiming SDVOSB status, provide documentation that shows the Service Disable Veteran (SDV) unconditionally owns 51 % of the business, controls the management and daily operations, and holds the highest officer position in the company. Documentation should also be provided to show that the SDV has a service-connected disability that has been determined by the Department of Defense or Department of Veteran Affairs. Finally, provide documentation that shows the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming VOSB status, provide documentation that shows the Veteran unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operation, make long-term decisions for the business, and holds the highest officer position in the company that works at the business fulltime during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming EDWOSB status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned by one or more women who are "economically disadvantaged", and primarily managed by an economically disadvantaged woman that make long-term decisions for the business, hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full-time during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000.00 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000.00, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million. � If claiming Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. The women must be U.S. citizens. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming Small Business status, provide documentation to show the business is small under NAICS code 336611. 1. Statement of Proposal Submission: Statement on how your company will do the work and that your company WILL submit a proposal as a prime contractor if a solicitation is issued as a result of this Sources Sought Notice. 2. Past Performance Information: Evidence of experience in work similar in type and scope to include contract numbers, project titles, and dollar amounts, points of contact and telephone numbers. If two companies are planning to conduct business and submit an offer as a Joint Venture or similar type of teaming agreement, they are requested to provide past performance information on projects of similar scope that they have performed together as a Joint Venture, if available. Providing individual past performance documentation from each company on separate projects where the two did not work together may be considered less relevant. title: USACE National Enterprise Dredging Center Scope Dredge to Budget Contract
description: Dashboard link: https://geo-essayons.egis.usace.army.mil/portal/apps/experiencebuilder/experience/?id=1b5c149b77d04afa8aa97160476258d4 DRAFT RFP ADDED Special Notice: W912PM27RA006 Title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget will occur on 16 October 2026 from 0900ET to 13:00ET via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing Scope Dredge to Budget acquisition strategy. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 15 October 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026. There will also be a face-to-face meeting with individual contractors that have the required equipment and intend to propose on this future solicitation. The face-to-face meetings will be on 03-04 November in Galveston, TX. Please respond to to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil of your interest in a face-to-face meeting no later than 24 September 2026 at 1PM ET.

Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. The Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) intends to issue a one year and two 6-month options, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) sole source contract to Noblis. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement demonstrating the ability to provide the requested services, which shall be considered by the Agency before the intended award date. Description of effort: Provide advisory and assistance services (A&AS) to the DoW Cooperative Threat Reduction (CTR) Program in managing and executing programs across the Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) spectrum as part of the broader countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD) mission. The A&AS provides the necessary expertise in achieving key U.S. national security objectives, as outlined in the National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and the DoD CWMD Strategy through subject matter experts (SMEs) in the applicable technical, international agreements, foreign partner country regulatory, foreign partner program sustainment, integrated product team and working group, acquisition, logistics management, financial, strategic planning, training, information technology, security, and administrative support. This contract is intended to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of the DoW CTR Program�s critical mission through the award of a bridge contract to continue external professional A&AS specialized support and technical expertise.

title: Bulk Propane Delivery Services - Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam, Washington
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE W912DW27X1CUL Bulk Propane Delivery Services � Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam, Washington NAICS Code: 325120 � Industrial Gas Manufacturing THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is not a solicitation, request for quotation, request for proposal, or commitment by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) to issue a solicitation, award a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in responding. 1. Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle District, is conducting market research to identify responsible and capable sources that can provide bulk propane delivery services to the following Government facilities in Washington State: Howard Hanson Dam, 36932 SE Green River Headworks Road, Ravensdale, WA 98051 Mud Mountain Dam, 30525 SE Mud Mountain Road, Enumclaw, WA 98022-8010 USACE anticipates establishing one or more commercial Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) to support recurring propane requirements. The Government anticipates placing BPA calls as needed for tank refills during the BPA ordering period. The Government is using NAICS 325120, Industrial Gas Manufacturing, for purposes of this market research. Interested parties should identify the NAICS code(s) and size standard under which they consider themselves eligible for this requirement. 2. Anticipated Requirement The anticipated requirement is for the delivery of commercial bulk propane to Government-owned or Government-designated propane tanks at Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam. The anticipated services may include: - Routine bulk propane deliveries as requested by the Government; - Emergency and/or after-hours propane deliveries; - Delivery to multiple sites under individual BPA calls; - Delivery-ticket documentation showing, at a minimum, date and time of delivery, delivery location, quantity delivered in gallons, unit price, applicable fees, and total price; - Compliance with applicable safety, transportation, environmental, and site-access requirements; - Coordination with designated Government points of contact; - Optional tank-level monitoring or vendor-managed delivery services, if commercially available and proposed. The Government anticipates that refill quantities, timing, and annual consumption may vary based on weather, operational requirements, and tank capacity. The Government does not guarantee any minimum quantity of propane or minimum number of calls. Estimated annual gallons, anticipated tank sizes, historical usage data, delivery access information, and anticipated BPA ordering period may be provided in any future solicitation, if issued. 3. Market Research Information Requested Interested parties are requested to provide a capability statement addressing the following: A. Company Information 1. Company name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact. 2. Point-of-contact name, title, telephone number, and email address. 3. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 4. CAGE code, if applicable. 5. Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 325120, including, as applicable: - Small business; - Small disadvantaged business; - Woman-owned small business; - HUBZone small business; - Service-disabled veteran-owned small business; and/or - Veteran-owned small business. 6. Identify any applicable GSA Schedule, Governmentwide Acquisition Contract, existing BPA, or other Federal contract vehicle through which the company currently provides propane or related fuel-delivery services. B. Capability and Service Coverage 1. Describe the company�s experience providing bulk propane delivery services to commercial, municipal, Federal, industrial, remote, or critical-infrastructure customers. 2. State whether the company can provide service to: - Howard Hanson Dam; and - Mud Mountain Dam. 3. Identify the normal service area, dispatch location(s), and approximate distance or travel time to each dam location. 4. Identify whether the company can provide tank-level monitoring, automatic refill, telemetry, or other inventory-management support. Describe any associated equipment, fees, data access, maintenance responsibilities, and cybersecurity or connectivity considerations. C. Commercial Pricing Practices The Government is particularly interested in understanding commercial pricing practices for propane deliveries in western Washington. Please address the following: 1. Describe how the company establishes its bulk propane prices for commercial or government customers. 2. Identify whether the company uses a published propane-price index, rack price, wholesale market index, or other objective benchmark. 3. If an index is used, identify: - The name of the index or publication; - The geographic market point or terminal; - The frequency of publication; - The date used to determine the price�for example, date of order, date before delivery, date of delivery, or another defined date; and - Whether the index value is available to the Government for invoice verification. 4. Identify any non-commodity charges that may apply, including: - Delivery fees; - Site-specific delivery fees; - Fuel or transportation surcharges; - Hazmat, environmental, or administrative fees; - Minimum-delivery charges; - Emergency or after-hours fees; - Tank rental, lease, maintenance, or monitoring fees; - Taxes; and - Any other recurring or one-time charges. 5. Describe whether these charges can be proposed as fixed rates for the BPA ordering period. E. Contracting and BPA Input 1. Identify any recommended BPA terms, ordering procedures, delivery requirements, pricing methods, or commercial practices the Government should consider. F. Response Instructions Interested parties shall submit a capability statement of no more than five (5) pages, excluding attachments, in PDF format. Responses shall be emailed to: Contract Specialist: Monique Paano Email: Monique.a.paano@usace.army.mil Subject Line: �Sources Sought Response � Bulk Propane Delivery � Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam� Responses are due no later than November 9, 2026 at noon Pacific Time. G. Important Notice This notice is issued solely for market-research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information, material, or costs associated with responding to this notice. The Government may use the information received to refine its requirements, determine the appropriate competition and small-business strategy, establish pricing and ordering procedures, and decide whether to pursue one or more BPAs for this requirement. The Small Business Programs Office POC for this requirement is: Enshane� Nomoto (she/her) Office of Small Business Programs enshane.nomoto@usace.army.mil

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. title: Coyote Valley Dam (CVD) Lake Mendocino Sewage and Septic Services
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE for a Market Research ONLY to determine the availability of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential future acquisition. The purpose of this NOTICE is to gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following categories: Small Business, Certified 8a, Certified HUB Zone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), for a Service Contract for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), San Francisco District. The capabilities will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining to Set-Aside for the Small Business Community or to conduct as an Other Than Small Business Procurement. Other than small businesses may respond to this NOTICE in the event the market does not indicate SB interest, however, preference will be given to the SB categories listed above. The government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Contractor shall provide all manpower, labor, equipment, materials/supplies, transportation, fuel, tools, supervision and other items and services necessary to provide sewage pumping and proper disposal, drain clearing, portable toilet rental, and portable/vault toilet stall cleaning/treatment services for the recreation areas designated for public use at Coyote Valley Dam and Lake Mendocino in Ukiah, California. The Period of Performance is anticipated to be 1 Base Year and 3 Option years. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or around December 2026. An official synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on beta.sam.gov and inviting firms to register electronically to receive a copy of the solicitation when it is issued. Requirements Overview 5.1 Basic Services: Sewage pumping and drain clearing is directly related to public health and sanitation and is essential to CVD/ Lake Mendocino�s recreation mission. The Contractor shall furnish all equipment, supplies, items, labor, materials, and services necessary to for sewage pumping and proper disposal, drain clearing, portable toilet rental, and portable/vault toilet stall cleaning/treatment in accordance with all federal, state, and local regulations. 5.2 Service Descriptions: 5.2.1 Lift Stations & Holding Tanks: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank (including all litter and refuse such as bottles, trash bags, clothing, etc.), and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Tank capacities throughout the park vary from 1,000 � 10,000 gallons. Tank locations are outlined in Attachment 1 Work Site Area & Sewage Locations. 5.2.2 Vault Toilets: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank/vault. This includes all litter and refuse (bottles, cans, trash bags, clothing, etc.), which can be a common occurrence in the public vault toilets at Lake Mendocino. The Contractor shall also recharge the tank/vault with approximately one foot of water after pumping, apply an enzyme treatment if needed, and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. An enzyme treatment may be needed to control odor and maintain cleanliness of the stall. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Vault toilets have a capacity of 1,000 gallons per stall. Vault toilet locations are outlined in Attachment 1. 5.2.3 Sewer and Drain Line Clearing: The Contractor shall provide any combination of video camera services, snaking, rooting, hydro-jetting, and/or chemical treatment necessary to identify and remedy drain line clogs such that the lines can flow freely. Lines that do not continue to flow freely for one week (7 days) will require re-work at no additional cost to the Government. 5.2.4 Portable Toilets: 5.2.4.1 Amount, Type, and Condition: Locations subject to portable toilet placement include recreation areas outlined in Attachment 1. This will primarily be in areas with flush restrooms that occasionally experience system failures. The Contractor shall have enough inventory 15 available to be able to provide up to four (4) sets of portable toilets at one time. A set includes one regular size portable toilet and one ADA-compliant size portable toilet. Portable toilets shall be for outdoor-use and anchorable. The Contractor shall maintain portables that are clean and in good repair, free of significant odors, damage, and vandalism. Stalls must have adequate ventilation, be uniformly painted, constructed such that walls provide adequate privacy, and have doors with a working lock mechanism. Portables should be delivered and placed on flat, level ground surfaces as directed by the COR. In the event portables are vandalized, damaged, and/or moved by the public, the Contractor bears the responsibility of retrieving, repairing and/or replacing them. At the discretion of the COR, the Contractor shall remove and replace damaged portables with ones in good condition. There are also two (2) USACE-owned portable toilets that are subject to service. The Contractor is not responsible for the good working condition of these portables but is required to follow the same service description outlined below in Section 5.2.4.3 for the same unit price as the Contractor-owned portables. 5.2.4.2 Rental Period: The Contractor shall deliver portable toilets in good working conditions within 48 hours of request by the COR. Portable toilets will be rented per type per two-week (15-day) period. 5.2.4.3 Service: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each portable, transport the waste from CVD/ Lake Mendocino, and dispose of it in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Additionally, each portable should be recharged with an industry standard deodorant/cleaner, restocked with reasonably enough toilet paper to last until the next service, and thoroughly cleaned. Cleaning includes scrubbing, wiping, rinsing, removing with appropriate soaps, disinfectants, and cleaning solutions to ensure stall floors, walls, ceilings, door, toilet lids, and toilet risers are free from waste, refuse, residues, spider webs, and significant odors. The area should be hosed down around the portables if needed to ensure any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. 5.3 Frequency: The Contractor shall provide services on a call-out basis. Scheduling for services will be agreed upon between the Contractor and the COR prior to the delivery of services. The allotted quantities for each service per this contract are based on field experiences from the past five (5) years and best estimates for future needs. An example schedule can be found in Attachment 2 Sample Service Schedule. 5.4 Line Items: 1) Lift Station/Holding Tank Pumping | Unit: Gallon a. Offerors should provide a quote per gallon of sewage pump, incorporating any additional costs (litter removal, sewage disposal) into the per gallon quote. 2) Vault Toilet Pumping & Treatment | Unit: Gallon a. Offerors should provide a quote per gallon of sewage pump, incorporating any additional costs (litter removal, recharging/treatment services, sewage disposal) 16 into the per gallon quote. 3) Sewer and Drain Line Clear Out | Unit: Job a. description: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS REGIONAL PROCUREMENT OFFICE (RPO) WEST NETWORK CONTRACTING OFFICE 17 (NCO 17) 5441 Babcock Road, Suite 302, San Antonio, TX 78240 SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Energy Center Steam Header and Boiler Valve, Gasket, and Vent Line Replacement VA North Texas Health Care System Dallas VA Medical Center, Dallas, Texas NOTICE INFORMATION Notice ID 36C25727Q0078 Notice Type Sources Sought (Market Research) Posted Date October 30, 2026 Response Deadline November 9, 2026, 2:00 p.m. Central Time Contracting Office Department of Veterans Affairs, RPO West | NCO 17 | Lab Services Support (LSS), 5441 Babcock Road, Suite 302, San Antonio, TX 78240 Primary Point of Contact Ognian D. Ivanov, Contract Officer, ognian.ivanov@va.gov Classification Code (PSC) J048 Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment Valves NAICS Code 238220 Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors Small Business Size Standard $19.0 million average annual receipts Set-Aside Status Total set-aside anticipated: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) VA VETS First Program Place of Performance Dallas VA Medical Center, Energy Center (Building 70), 4500 S. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216 1. PURPOSE This is a Sources Sought notice issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) West, Network Contracting Office 17 (NCO 17), in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, Market Research. This notice is issued for information and market research purposes only. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), an Invitation for Bid (IFB), a Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an offer by the Government to contract for any supplies or services. This notice is not a commitment by the Government to award a contract, and the Government will not reimburse any respondent for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Responses to this notice are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right not to set aside this requirement or to otherwise change its acquisition strategy based on the results of this market research. 2. BACKGROUND AND DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUIREMENT The VA North Texas Health Care System (VANTHCS), Dallas VA Medical Center, requires the replacement of valves, gaskets, and vent lines on the main steam header and on Boilers 1, 2, and 3 located at the Energy Center, Building 70, 4500 S. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216. The existing valves are the original 1994 installation, and the age of the system has precluded effective maintenance and upkeep. Replacement valves and piping shall meet or exceed the specifications of the current installation and shall conform to applicable steam industry standards and regulations. The contractor shall provide all labor, supplies, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and management necessary to remove, purchase, install, and test the valves, gaskets, and vent lines on the main steam header and boilers. Key elements of the work include: Coordinating equipment shutdown with the facility representative / Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) prior to commencing work; Performing required lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures on affected equipment; Removing existing valves, vent lines, and associated components; Inspecting the interior of the main steam header body and checking the drip leg for blockages; Cleaning flange faces and installing new spiral-wound gaskets; Installing new steam valves with steam balancing and vent lines using Schedule 80 carbon steel piping and full-port ball valves (three-piece bolted, disassemble for internal component access without unthreading from the supply line); Installing new removable high-temperature insulation jackets on all steam valves; Replacing the boiler steam stop, isolation, and vent valves with new vent piping on Boilers 1, 2, and 3; and Performing leak checks, with the assistance of the COR and Utilities Systems Operator (USO), during boiler startup and campus pressurization to 110 psi. The Government anticipates a firm-fixed-price contract awarded under FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE VA North Texas Health Care System, Dallas VA Medical Center, Energy Center (Building 70), 4500 S. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216. 4. SDVOSB AND VOSB SET-ASIDE INTENT This requirement is anticipated to be set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) concerns in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) Subpart 819.70, VA s VETS First Program, implemented under the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127(d) and 8127(e). This Sources Sought notice is issued in part to determine whether there are two or more responsible, capable SDVOSB or VOSB firms that can perform this requirement, and to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy. To be eligible for award under the anticipated set-aside, a firm must: Be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of response and award; Hold a current certification from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as an SDVOSB or VOSB in accordance with 13 CFR Part 128; and Meet the small business size standard for NAICS code 238220 ($19.0 million average annual receipts). 5. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INTERESTED FIRMS Interested SDVOSB and VOSB firms are requested to submit a capability package that includes the following: Company Information: Legal business name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE code, physical and mailing addresses, website, and primary point of contact (name, title, telephone number, and email address); Business Status and Certifications: Small business size under NAICS 238220, SBA SDVOSB or VOSB certification status (including certification number and expiration date, if applicable), and any other socio-economic designations held; Relevant Experience: A description of comparable work performed within the past three (3) years involving steam distribution systems, steam headers, boiler plants, industrial piping, or similar mechanical/plumbing construction and maintenance. Include contract or task order numbers, the contracting activity or commercial customer, dollar value, period of performance, and whether the work was performed as a prime contractor or subcontractor; Technical Capability and Staffing: A description of the firm s capability, key personnel, and capacity to perform work of this type and magnitude at the Dallas VA Medical Center, including any applicable state of Texas licenses, welding certifications, or qualifications held by the firm or its personnel; Comments: Any comments or feedback regarding the scope of work, proposed NAICS code, anticipated contract structure, or other aspects of the planned acquisition. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS AND DEADLINE Responses must be submitted electronically via email to Ognian D. Ivanov, Contract Officer, at ognian.ivanov@va.gov . Use the following subject line: Sources Sought Steam Header and Boiler Valve Replacement [Company Name]. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 p.m. Central Time on November 9, 2026. Responses shall not exceed ten (10) pages in total (including all attachments) and shall be submitted in Microsoft Word or PDF format. Questions regarding this notice shall be submitted in writing via email to the point of contact listed above. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. Responses submitted after the deadline or to any other email address may not be considered. 7. IMPORTANT NOTICES This Sources Sought notice is issued solely for information, planning, and market research purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. title: Loaded Cartridge Assembly (MC91) for MK 5 Mod ) Explosive Bolt
description: This announcement should not be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. The U.S. Navy does not intend to award a contract based on this Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice. THIS IS NOT A Request for a Proposal AND DOES NOT OBLIGATE THE U.S. GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE an RFP. This RFI is for U.S. Government planning purposes only and constitutes requests for exchange of information pursuant to FAR Part 10. The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Department, Code 02 is conducting Market Research on the Loaded Cartridge Assembly, DODIC MC91. NSWC IHD is conducting a market survey to identify sources/vendors capable of supplying the MC91 cartridge satisfying the following requirements: 1. The cartridge needs to meet the criteria specified by WS6061 and WS6052, ADL 2429839, their lower-tier documents, and be compatible with the MK 5 MOD 0 Explosive Bolt (M254), a critical component on the AN/BST-1 Buoy system. The Technical Data Package (TDP) contains technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C., Sec 2751, et seq.). To receive the TDP, interested vendors must submit a written request accompanied by an approved DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement), signed NDA, and active CAGE code. 2. Contractor must be able to stand up a manufacturing line and be able to support the U.S. Government by providing all deliveries within one year of award. 3. Procurement includes production units (QTY 100) as well as all associated destructive test samples required for qualification and acceptance. This procurement includes the manufacture, testing (including nondestructive testing (NDT/radiographic) capabilities), packaging, and delivery of the MC91 Cartridge Assembly. Request your company provide responses to the following questionnaire: Does your company have a production line available that can meet the requirements mentioned above? If yes, describe your company's history and experience with supplying this item (or similar cartridges for explosive bolts) including the total number supplied to date and how the facilities are ready to support USG requirements. What is your company�s availability of inert metal parts or existing validated energetic loading lines? If the MC91 cartridges are not currently in stock, when would they be available for delivery? How many days or months after an award? Can your Company provide the rate of production the manufacturing facility is capable of per year? Can your company provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit price estimate based on the stated quantity of 100 production units plus required test samples, along with estimated stepped pricing for higher production rates? Do test reports exist that demonstrate the MC91 (or similar cartridges for explosive bolts) manufacturing accuracy and reliability? Actual reports are not required to be submitted as part of this request for information but will be accepted after your initial response to this request. Are you able to supply documented ability of your company's MC91 cartridges to function reliably with the MK 5 MOD 0 Explosive Bolt? Does your facility hold the necessary ATF licensing, Net Explosive Weight (NEW) storage capacity, and compliance with DoD 4145.26-M to manufacture, assemble, and store loaded MC91 cartridges? Describe your inspection capabilities for energetic components, specifically hermetic seal testing (helium leak rate) and real-time radiography (X-ray) for internal explosive pellet/column alignment. What are the lead times for primary energetic ingredients/mixes and specialized metal hardware required by WS6061 and WS6052? Are any materials obsolete or sole-sourced? Does your company possess or capability to produce all tooling, crimping dies, and electrical/bridgewire resistance test fixtures required to manufacture this item, or would Government-Furnished Equipment/Tooling (GFE/GFT) be required? Small Business Subcontracting & Nonmanufacturer Rule Compliance: If responding as a Small Business prime under NAICS 325920, please clarify your manufacturing approach: Does your company intend to perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding material costs) in-house at your own safety-approved facility? If you do not manufacture the cartridges in-house, do you intend to source the MC91 cartridges from another domestic small business manufacturer? If you intend to partner with a large business manufacturer, are you aware of the requirements to obtain an individual SBA Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR) waiver prior to solicitation close? All interested sources shall provide the organization name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, business size, Unique Entity ID, and CAGE Code. In addition, all interested sources shall provide a summary of their company�s capabilities and delivery timeframe and schedule. All responding sources must email their response submissions no later than 17:00 Eastern Time on November 9, 2026 to the Point of Contacts (POCs) listed below. Submissions must be in PDF format and shall not exceed fifteen (15) pages in total. 1) NSWC IHD Attn: Michael Persinger Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806 Michael.a.persinger2.civ@us.navy.mil 2) NSWC IHD Attn: Gerardo Ilaria Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 gerardo.ilaria.civ@us.navy.mil
